newsitem.title: INDIA: India mourns Deng, praises him for reviving ties.
newsitem.headline: India mourns Deng, praises him for reviving ties.

text.p: India on Thursday mourned the death of Chinese patriarch Deng Xiaoping, saying he was largely responsible for improving ties between the two Asian giants.

"We express our heartfelt grief at the death of the great personality," Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral told Reuters. "He not only shaped the destiny of his nation but contributed directly to building good relations between our two countries."

Indian newspapers had splashed pictures of a long handshake in Beijing in 1988 between Deng and then Indian prime minister Rajiv Gandhi when the two countries ended years of suspicion following a brief border war in 1962.
"That was a historic moment which determined the course of our future relations," Gujral said.
Chinese President Jiang Zemin, Deng's anointed successor, visited India last year. Analysts said Jiang's expected promotion would make him China's first paramount leader to have visited India.
"Jiang's visit was a great boost to the continuing process of peace and reconciliation," Gujral said. "His presence as a key player will naturally help our ties."
